title: 🗄️ Data Model
help: A live, introspected map of everything AgentCase actually holds — not a diagram somebody drew once and forgot to update, but tables each read directly off the running registries, field lists and file writers at the moment you open them. If a field is added, renamed or removed in the code, this page reflects it on the next reload with
. That is the whole design point: a data-model page that can drift from the code is worse than no page at all, because it teaches the wrong thing with total confidence.

🔍 Why four separate tables, not one
These are genuinely different kinds of data with different failure modes. A
can be deleted and the menu simply loses a tab. A
missing from the registry is a silent data-loss bug — the field looks fine until the user reloads. A
is read-only and derived, so it can never itself be wrong, only mis-bound. A

is a literal embedded in a formula, and the entire "tier 1/2/3 audit" work earlier in this build existed because those used to be invisible. Collapsing them into one table would hide exactly the distinction that makes each one worth checking.

Nothing on this page is hand-maintained data. Every row is read live from what it documents — the zone registry, the live case, the variable registry (

Pure documentation. No control here writes to the model — this page only reads. To change a coefficient, use the section it links to; to change what persists, change the type and its runtime twin in code (and add a file migration when the shape changes), a deliberate barrier against casually breaking save/restore.
